markets.rules_primary: If the certified percentage of the popular vote received by James Fishback in the 2026 Florida Republican gubernatorial primary is 15% to 100%, inclusive of both endpoints, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The percentage is calculated as (total votes received by the specified person/party ÷ total valid votes cast) × 100, rounded to the specified decimal places. Resolution is based on certified/official results only, not preliminary results. Write-in votes are included if they appear in certified results. Invalid, spoiled, or rejected ballots are excluded from both numerator and denominator. If multiple rounds of voting occur (e.g., ranked choice voting), the percentage is based on the specified round or the first round if not specified. If the election is cancelled, postponed beyond the market expiration, or no certified results are available by expiration, the market resolves to No. If a recount changes the certified percentage before expiration, the most recent certified percentage is used.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the House has conducted any recorded vote on legislation that would materially restrict birth tourism or birthright citizenship for children of temporary visitors after Issuance and before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This includes:
Roll call votes
Recorded votes
Yea-and-nay votes
Electronic votes (in the House)
Division/standing votes

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:
Voice votes where individual member positions are not recorded
Unanimous consent agreements without a recorded vote
Votes in committee, unless the bill/motion specifically refers to a committee vote
Procedural determinations by the presiding officer
Deemed passage without an actual vote

For clarity:
A vote on cloture regarding the bill/motion, including cloture on a motion to proceed to the bill/motion, DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on the rule governing debate of the bill/motion DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion if the bill/motion specifically refers to that rule
A vote on a motion to proceed to the bill/motion DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on final passage DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion
A vote on an amendment to the bill/motion does NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion unless the bill/motion specifically refers to that amendment
markets.title: Will the House vote on legislation that would materially restrict birth tourism or birthright citizenship for children of temporary visitors?

markets.rules_secondary: This market resolves based on whether the price ($/lb) of Chemical Lean Beef Trim, as published by USDA, meets or exceeds the specified strike value at any point during the time period. The relevant data source is the USDA AMS National/Regional Weekly Boneless Processing Beef and Beef Trimmings report. A single qualifying weekly print at or above a given strike is sufficient to resolve that strike to Yes; no further crossings are required. If a given week's report shows zero reported trades or a $0.00 weighted average for this grade, that week's data will be treated as unavailable, and the most recently available valid weekly value will be used in its place for purposes of determining whether the strike was met. If no valid data is available for the entire time period, all markets resolve to No. Prices are denominated in USD per hundredweight (lb) and rounded to two decimal places. Unless otherwise specified, prices reflect USDA's reported FOB Plant negotiated sales basis and exclude any additional handling, freight, or transaction fees. Any revisions or corrections to a weekly report published after that report's initial release will not affect market resolution.

markets.rules_primary: If the number of people who have served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, excluding Keir Starmer, after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2029 is above 5, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
"Served in the role" means that an individual has formally held the position in an official capacity, whether by appointment, election, succession, or acting designation, and performed the duties of that role for any length of time during the time period. If an individual serves multiple non-consecutive terms in the role, they will count once for each term (allowing an individual to be counted multiple times). If an individual holds the role temporarily in an "acting" or "interim" capacity for any amount of time, or is formally designated as such, they count as serving in the role. Dual officeholders count once per person even if holding multiple titles simultaneously.

If an individual is appointed but never sworn in, or withdraws before assuming office, they do not count as serving. Vacancies do not count as individuals serving. Posthumous designations or honorary titles do not count.
